author: Jimmy Parker
title: Brandon Gill Turns Abdul El-Sayed's Reparations Talk Back on Him [VIDEO]
text:
El-Sayed Dodges the Simple Question
Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed found himself in a rough spot after his appearance Monday night on Jesse Watters’ Fox News show, where Watters pressed him on whether he supports reparations for slavery. Instead of giving a clean yes-or-no answer, El-Sayed leaned into the familiar political fog machine and said, “I think we need to have an honest conversation about the incredible debt that was put upon black folks,” adding, “I just think that’s fair.” Watters pushed back by asking, “Reparations. You support that?” and later said, “We have you on the record as backing it.” That is when the dance got even more noticeable, because voters can usually tell when a politician is trying to answer without actually answering. Funny how “honest conversation” often shows up right when a straight answer leaves the room.
https://x.com/RNCResearch/status/2092055581825605935?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw
The Earlier Video Said the Quiet Part Out Loud
The problem for El-Sayed is that an older clip from May surfaced, showing him speaking at a town hall in Detroit and using much clearer language than he offered on Fox News. In that video, El-Sayed said, “And we owe the reparations of recognizing that this country was built on the uncompensated labor of enslaved people.” He continued, “I believe that we owe it to engage in reparations,” then added, “We need to invest in reparations. We need reparations in this country.” That is not exactly a mystery novel. The record shows one version on television, where he avoided a direct answer, and another version in Detroit, where he plainly called for reparations. Voters may disagree on the policy, but they deserve to know what a candidate actually believes before they are asked to hand him power.
https://x.com/WesternLensman/status/2092092870798843957?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw
Brandon Gill Asks the Question Democrats Hate
Rep. Brandon Gill, a Texas Republican, responded to the resurfaced video with a pointed question aimed right at the logic behind El-Sayed’s position. Gill wrote on X, “Does Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed also think that the Arab nations his ancestors come from owe reparations, since just as many Africans were enslaved in the Arab world as in the Americas?” That question cuts through the usual campaign chatter because it asks whether the reparations standard is being applied evenly or only when it fits the preferred political script. The left loves sweeping moral lectures until someone asks whether the same rules apply to everyone. Then suddenly the room gets quieter than a Biden press conference after staff calls time.
https://x.com/realBrandonGill/status/2092436367234228539?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw
The Kafala Issue Adds Another Layer
The source also pointed to reporting from DW.com about modern slavery concerns in parts of the Arab Gulf region, specifically involving the “kafala” system. According to the cited description, millions of migrant workers can face harsh conditions with little or no pay, while employers are able to hire unskilled workers from places such as Africa and South Asia. The practice can also involve workers giving up their passports and losing the ability to leave the country or change jobs without employer permission. That matters here because Gill’s question was not just a cheap jab, it raised a broader issue about whether historical guilt is being discussed honestly or selectively. If El-Sayed is going to campaign on reparations and “honest conversation,” then the next interview should include honest questions about the wider history and present-day abuses tied to slavery and forced labor.

JIMMY
